authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, enhancing effective coherence times.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of energy relaxation errors in superconducting qubits by converting them into erasure errors that can be detected and corrected more efficiently.
method: The authors leverage the parity symmetry of integer fluxonium qubits and implement a dispersive readout scheme that maps relaxation events to detectable erasures.
result: They demonstrate that energy relaxation errors are converted into erasures, significantly boosting the effective coherence times of the qubits.
conclusion: This erasure conversion technique offers a practical path to fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting circuits, and can be integrated with existing quantum error correction codes.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, enabling coherent cancellation of backaction noise.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a new method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a mode-multiplexing technique using a single optical cavity to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but suffer from slow gate speeds; cavity enhancement can speed up operations, but scaling to many atoms is challenging. This work aims to overcome the scalability bottleneck by multiplexing cavity modes.
method: The authors introduce a scheme where multiple cavity modes (e.g., Hermite-Gaussian or Laguerre-Gaussian modes) are used to simultaneously address different atoms in an array, leveraging the spatial structure of the modes to achieve parallel operations.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms that can be processed in parallel without sacrificing cavity enhancement, potentially enabling fast gates in large arrays.
conclusion: This approach provides a path toward scalable cavity-enhanced quantum operations in neutral-atom platforms, which is relevant for quantum computing and simulation. Future work includes experimental implementation and optimization of mode addressing.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstration of >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: To achieve the high fidelities required for fault-tolerant quantum computing, simultaneous high-fidelity operations across all qubit functionalities must be demonstrated in a single device.
method: The authors optimized qubit-coupler interactions and developed a new calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors, enabling high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit CZ gates, and readout on the same superconducting chip.
result: They achieved >99.9% fidelity for all three operations: single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout, setting a new benchmark for superconducting quantum processors.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that superconducting qubits can meet the fidelity thresholds for surface code error correction, paving the way for scalable quantum computing. Future work will focus on integrating more qubits and improving coherence.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for precise Hamiltonian simulation. This work aims to reduce that overhead.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized time evolution, where the Hamiltonian simulation step uses randomized product formulas that are only partially randomized, balancing accuracy and cost.
result: They demonstrate that this approach yields orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard deterministic methods.
conclusion: The technique makes quantum phase estimation more practical for near-term quantum devices, with implications for quantum chemistry and other applications.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Haar-random quantum codes exhibit a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise, with a simple mechanism governing the transition.
motivation: Understanding the performance and limitations of quantum error-correcting codes under realistic noise is crucial for building reliable quantum computers and communication networks.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics methods, mapping the decoding problem to a spin model and studying spectral properties to identify phase transitions.
result: They find a clear transition between decodable and non-decodable phases as a function of noise strength and code parameters, with the transition point determined by the spectral gap of the code's density matrix.
conclusion: The results provide a simple criterion for code performance and suggest design principles for optimal quantum codes, with implications for quantum communication and fault-tolerant computation.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid oscillator-qudit systems, introducing new stabilizer states and error-correcting codes for continuous-variable and discrete-variable hybrid platforms.
motivation: To unify discrete- and continuous-variable quantum information processing under a common stabilizer framework, enabling scalable error correction and improved sensing protocols.
method: The authors develop a symplectic formalism for hybrid systems, define stabilizer states and codes using noncommutative geometry, and characterize symplectic operations.
result: New classes of hybrid stabilizer states and error-correcting codes are constructed, with potential advantages for displacement sensing and fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for hybrid quantum processors, paving the way for experimental implementations in systems like superconducting circuits coupled to spin ensembles.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling in bosonic systems and demonstrates that non-Gaussian operations can surpass these limits, enabling colder states.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes to near ground states is crucial for quantum technologies, but the role of Gaussian vs. non-Gaussian resources in achieving low temperatures was not well understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on Gaussian constraints and quantify the minimal achievable temperature under Gaussian operations, then show how non-Gaussian resources (e.g., photon subtraction) can overcome these bounds.
result: Gaussian operations impose a fundamental cooling limit, but non-Gaussian operations can achieve arbitrarily low temperatures in principle, with practical enhancements demonstrated for specific protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a clear thermodynamic classification of cooling resources and suggests that non-Gaussian operations are essential for reaching ultracold regimes in bosonic quantum devices.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hardware-friendly quantum Gibbs sampling protocol using local circuits that achieves rapid mixing and accuracy without block encoding.
motivation: Quantum Gibbs sampling is crucial for many quantum algorithms, but existing methods often require complex operations like block encoding, which are challenging to implement on near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors replace block encoding with local circuits, designing a thermalization protocol that relies on local interactions and a specific mixing strategy to prepare Gibbs states efficiently.
result: The protocol demonstrates rapid mixing and high accuracy in preparing Gibbs states, with rigorous bounds on the mixing time and error, and is compatible with current quantum hardware constraints.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway for quantum Gibbs sampling on near-term devices, with implications for quantum simulation and optimization, and opens avenues for further hardware-efficient thermalization algorithms.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental limits on information storage and transmission in quantum memories under Markovian noise using information-theoretic tools.
motivation: To understand the ultimate capabilities of noisy quantum memories for storing and transmitting quantum information, which is crucial for quantum communication and computation.
method: The authors employ information-theoretic analysis, likely using entropy accumulation or related techniques, to characterize the effects of Markovian noise on quantum memory.
result: Key findings include bounds on storage time and transmission fidelity under Markovian noise, possibly establishing trade-offs between noise strength and memory performance.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits that can guide the design of error correction and noise mitigation strategies in quantum memories, with implications for quantum repeaters and networks.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate dissipative quantum dynamics relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control of asymmetry in the oscillator.
motivation: To explore quantum simulation of chemical reactions using a superconducting circuit platform, specifically modeling activation processes that involve dissipation.
method: The authors employ a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator, a type of superconducting nonlinear resonator, and control its asymmetry to mimic the dissipative quantum system of a chemical reaction.
result: They demonstrate that the parametric oscillator can simulate key features of chemical activation, including the role of asymmetry and dissipation, with potential for scaling to more complex reactions.
conclusion: This work establishes a new quantum simulation platform for chemical dynamics, with implications for understanding reaction mechanisms and designing quantum-enhanced chemistry simulations.

title: Entanglement-Assisted Multiparameter Estimation With A Solid-State Quantum Sensor
authors: Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, And Paola Cappellaro
abstract:
Author(s): Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, and Paola Cappellaro

Entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin in experiment allows for concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020307] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates entanglement-assisted multiparameter estimation using a solid-state quantum sensor, enabling concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and precision of multiparameter estimation in quantum sensing by leveraging entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin.
method: Experimental implementation with a solid-state quantum sensor (likely NV center) where entanglement is created between the electronic spin and a nearby nuclear spin, followed by a tailored measurement sequence that extracts multiple parameters simultaneously.
result: Entanglement allows concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase with enhanced precision compared to classical schemes, demonstrating the advantage of quantum resources in multiparameter sensing.
conclusion: The work provides a practical demonstration of entanglement-enhanced multiparameter estimation in a solid-state platform, with implications for quantum sensing, metrology, and quantum information processing.

title: Hardware-Efficient Universal Linear Transformations For Optical Modes In The Synthetic Time Dimension
authors: Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Author(s): Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, and Saikat Guha

A synthetic time-domain photonic processor exponentially reduces hardware complexity while maintaining all-to-all connectivity, exceeding performance thresholds for scalable, universal quantum computation under realistic physical constraints.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020305] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: A synthetic time-domain photonic processor achieves universal linear transformations with exponentially reduced hardware complexity, enabling scalable quantum computation.
motivation: To overcome hardware scaling challenges in optical quantum computing by reducing the number of physical components while maintaining all-to-all connectivity.
method: The authors propose a photonic processor that uses a synthetic time dimension to implement universal linear transformations, leveraging time-multiplexed modes and a single nonlinear element.
result: The design achieves exponential reduction in hardware complexity compared to traditional spatial approaches, and exceeds performance thresholds for universal quantum computation under realistic noise and loss.
conclusion: This work paves the way for scalable, hardware-efficient optical quantum processors, with potential applications in quantum communication and computation.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a systematic classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols that go beyond quantum key distribution, addressing the growing need for diverse quantum-enhanced security tasks.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum money, quantum digital signatures, quantum secret sharing, quantum oblivious transfer) and discusses their theoretical security models and experimental implementations using photonic platforms.
result: It presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic protocols, highlights their security guarantees and limitations, and surveys current photonic experimental progress.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but many face practical challenges; future work should focus on improving efficiency, security proofs, and experimental scalability.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: This review classifies universal nonequilibrium stationary states in driven open quantum systems using quantum field theory, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal behavior lacks a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify stationary states based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking them to underlying symmetries and topological features.
conclusion: The classification provides a roadmap for understanding and engineering nonequilibrium phases, with implications for quantum technologies and thermodynamics.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is non-classical and non-quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To constrain possible theories of gravity beyond classical and quantum frameworks using quantum information methods.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and thought experiments for tabletop-scale tests of gravitationally induced entanglement between quantum probes.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are analyzed, showing potential to distinguish between classical, quantum, and other theories of gravity.
conclusion: Quantum information tools provide a concrete path to test the quantum nature of gravity, with near-term experimental prospects.

title: Boltzmann Sampling By Diabatic Quantum Annealing
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Yongjoo Baek
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Yongjoo Baek

Boltzmann sampling is a central component of many computational frameworks, including numerous algorithms in machine learning. Although quantum annealers have been investigated as potential fast Boltzmann samplers, their dependence on environmental noise makes precise control of the effective temper…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065302] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a diabatic quantum annealing protocol for Boltzmann sampling that enables precise control of effective temperature without relying on environmental noise.
motivation: Quantum annealers are promising for fast Boltzmann sampling, but their dependence on environmental noise makes precise temperature control difficult. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors introduce a diabatic quantum annealing protocol that uses controlled non-adiabatic transitions to achieve Boltzmann sampling at a desired effective temperature, analyzed via theoretical modeling and numerical simulations.
result: The protocol allows tuning of the effective temperature independently of the physical temperature, enabling accurate Boltzmann sampling across a range of temperatures.
conclusion: This work provides a new method for controlled Boltzmann sampling on quantum annealers, with potential applications in machine learning and optimization, and suggests further experimental validation.

title: Impossibility Of Quantum Private Queries
authors: Esther Hänggi And Severin Winkler
abstract:
Author(s): Esther Hänggi and Severin Winkler

This work investigates whether quantum communication protocols allow confidential access to a remote database. It shows that any protocol that does not reveal which item is retrieved allows the user to reconstruct the entire database.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022036] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Any quantum private query protocol that hides which item is retrieved allows the user to reconstruct the entire database, proving impossibility of such protocols.
motivation: To determine whether quantum communication can enable private database queries without revealing the queried item, which is a fundamental question in quantum cryptography.
method: The authors use information-theoretic arguments and quantum communication complexity to prove a lower bound showing that any protocol with perfect user privacy must leak the entire database.
result: They prove that no quantum protocol can simultaneously hide the queried item from the database and prevent the user from learning more than one item; the user can always reconstruct the full database.
conclusion: Quantum private queries are impossible, which has implications for designing secure quantum communication protocols and understanding the limits of quantum cryptography.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for understanding qubit leakage and improving readout in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Transmon qubits can ionize, escaping their computational states into highly excited states, which degrades performance. Understanding this process is essential for developing better readout schemes and error mitigation.
method: The authors experimentally probe transmon ionization using microwave spectroscopy and model the dynamics with Landau-Zener theory, analyzing multiphoton resonances that drive transitions to high-energy states.
result: They identify specific multiphoton resonance conditions that lead to ionization and characterize the transition rates, showing that ionization occurs via sequential Landau-Zener transitions through intermediate states.
conclusion: The findings provide a detailed understanding of transmon ionization, enabling design of readout protocols that avoid these loss channels, and open avenues for studying nonequilibrium dynamics in superconducting circuits.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A deep-level defect in ZnO with long coherence time and high spin selectivity enables high-fidelity single-shot readout for quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a solid-state spin defect in a wide-band-gap oxide that can serve as a scalable quantum platform, addressing the need for long coherence and high readout fidelity.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of the defect's electronic structure, spin properties, and electron-phonon coupling.
result: The defect exhibits an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO defects are a promising new platform for scalable quantum technologies, with potential for quantum sensing, communication, and computing.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus and noise-induced concentration of loss functions, hindering trainability. Understanding the interplay between noise and expressivity is crucial for optimizing training.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the concentration of loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, relating the variance of the loss to circuit expressivity and noise parameters.
result: They show that noise can both help and hinder training: while it reduces expressivity, it also bounds the variance of the loss, potentially alleviating barren plateaus. Quantitative estimates are provided.
conclusion: The results offer a roadmap for designing noise-resilient variational algorithms and suggest that moderate noise can be beneficial for trainability, with implications for near-term quantum computing.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
motivation: To accurately capture complex spatiotemporally correlated errors in transmon quantum processors, which are critical for reliable simulation and algorithm performance.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that accounts for correlated errors across multiple qubits and over time, and validate it using a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when used as a proxy simulator.
conclusion: This work provides a practical noise modeling framework that enhances the fidelity of quantum simulations on transmon processors, with implications for error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Overhead In Quantum Circuits With Time-Multiplexed Qubit Control
authors: Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, And Anton Frisk Kockum
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, and Anton Frisk Kockum

Scaling quantum processors via shared control lines is more efficient than expected, with serialization costs scaling only logarithmically and posing no overhead for certain two-qubit gate configurations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020308] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that time-multiplexed qubit control via shared lines incurs only logarithmic overhead, making it a scalable approach for quantum processors.
motivation: Scaling quantum processors requires efficient control of many qubits; shared control lines reduce hardware complexity but may introduce serialization overhead. The authors aimed to quantify this overhead.
method: The authors analyze quantum circuits with time-multiplexed control, modeling the serialization cost and its impact on circuit depth and gate fidelity. They consider different two-qubit gate configurations.
result: The overhead scales only logarithmically with the number of qubits, and for certain two-qubit gate configurations, there is no overhead at all.
conclusion: Time-multiplexed control is a viable path for scaling quantum processors without significant performance penalties, with implications for superconducting circuits and other platforms.

title: Single-Enantiomer Spin Polarizers In Superconducting Junctions
authors: Lorenz Meyer, Nicolas Néel, And Jörg Kröger
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenz Meyer, Nicolas Néel, and Jörg Kröger

A new experiment shows that spin-polarized currents conducted by helical organic molecules are not just a measurement artifact, as some researchers suspected.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226201] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Experiments demonstrate that helical organic molecules can act as spin polarizers in superconducting junctions, confirming that the observed spin-polarized currents are not artifacts.
motivation: There was controversy whether spin-polarized currents through helical organic molecules are genuine or measurement artifacts; this work aims to settle the debate.
method: The authors performed experiments with superconducting junctions incorporating helical organic molecules and measured spin-polarized transport properties.
result: They observed clear spin polarization in the current, ruling out artifact explanations and establishing the molecules as effective spin polarizers.
conclusion: The findings validate the use of helical molecules for spin injection in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in spintronics and quantum information.

title: Spin-Dependent Fluorescence Mediated By Antisymmetric Exchange In Triplet Exciton Pairs
authors: Yan Sun, G. Ricci, M. Monteverde, V. Derkach, T. Chanelière, E. Aldridge, D. Casanova, D. Beljonne, J. E. Anthony, And A. D. Chepelianskii
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Sun, G. Ricci, M. Monteverde, V. Derkach, T. Chanelière, E. Aldridge, D. Casanova, D. Beljonne, J. E. Anthony, and A. D. Chepelianskii

Singlet fission and triplet-triplet annihilation (TTA) are spin-dependent phenomena critical to optoelectronics. The dynamics of spin populations during geminate triplet pair separation are crucial for controlling fission and TTA rates. We show that the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) induce…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 216903] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in triplet exciton pairs can mediate spin-dependent fluorescence, offering a new mechanism to control singlet fission and triplet-triplet annihilation.
motivation: Understanding spin dynamics in geminate triplet pairs is crucial for optimizing optoelectronic devices that rely on singlet fission and TTA. The role of antisymmetric exchange (DMI) in these processes was previously unexplored.
method: The authors combine theoretical modeling with experimental measurements on organic semiconductors to demonstrate DMI-induced spin mixing and its effect on fluorescence.
result: DMI leads to spin-dependent fluorescence by mixing singlet and triplet states in triplet pairs, thereby influencing the rates of fission and TTA.
conclusion: This work identifies DMI as a key factor in spin-dependent photophysics, with implications for designing more efficient organic solar cells and light-emitting devices.

title: Localization And Scattering Of A Photon In Quasiperiodic Qubit Arrays
authors: Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, And Chaohong Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, and Chaohong Lee

We study the localization and scattering of a single photon in a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings. As the quasiperiodic strength increases, localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetime appear around the resonant frequency and form a continuum band. In stark c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063704] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies single-photon localization and scattering in waveguide-coupled qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings, revealing a continuum of long-lived subradiant states.
motivation: To understand how quasiperiodic disorder affects photon transport and localization in waveguide QED systems, which is relevant for quantum information processing and light-matter interfaces.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings, using a tight-binding model and solving for single-photon scattering and bound states.
result: As quasiperiodic strength increases, localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetimes emerge around the resonant frequency, forming a continuum band. These states are robust against disorder.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into controlling photon localization in quasiperiodic qubit arrays, with potential applications in quantum memory and slow-light devices.

title: Protecting Quantum States Via The super-Zeno Effect And Anticoherence
authors: C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, And L. Hanotel
abstract:
Author(s): C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, and L. Hanotel

The authors introduce a protocol that combines the quantum super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise arising from spin interactions of polynomial order =1 a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations, while a spin-/2 example achieves average fidelity with short-time scaling −F¯∝
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a protocol combining the super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to protect quantum states from polynomial-order spin interactions.
motivation: To develop a method for protecting quantum states against noise from spin interactions, which is crucial for quantum information processing.
method: The protocol uses the quantum super-Zeno effect (frequent projective measurements) and spin-anticoherent subspaces (states that are maximally sensitive to rotations) to suppress noise from polynomial-order spin operators.
result: For spin-1, a quantum gyroscope is achieved that protects states from unwanted rotations; for spin-1/2, average fidelity scales as 1 - F̄ ∝ t^4, showing improved protection.
conclusion: The combination of super-Zeno and anticoherence offers a new way to protect quantum states, with potential applications in quantum sensing and memory.

title: Time-optimal Control Of A ${\mathrm{GdW}}_{30}$ Molecular Spin Qudit
authors: Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, And Josep Maria Bofill
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, and Josep Maria Bofill

Quantum systems with more than two levels, known as qudits, offer enhanced information density and potentially more efficient quantum operations compared with traditional qubits. Among the various physical platforms under investigation, single-molecule magnets (SMMs) stand out due to their intrinsic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062603] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates time-optimal control of a GdW30 molecular spin qudit using optimal control theory, achieving high-fidelity gates for quantum information processing.
motivation: To exploit the larger Hilbert space of qudits for more efficient quantum operations, and to demonstrate control of molecular spin qudits as a platform for quantum computing.
method: The authors model the GdW30 molecule as a spin-7/2 qudit and apply optimal control theory (GRAPE algorithm) to design microwave pulses that implement single-qudit gates in minimal time while maintaining high fidelity.
result: They achieve time-optimal control pulses for a set of universal gates (e.g., Hadamard, T gate) with fidelities above 99.9% and gate times on the order of tens of nanoseconds.
conclusion: Molecular spin qudits are a viable platform for fast, high-fidelity quantum control, and optimal control techniques can be extended to larger qudits and multi-qudit systems.

title: Spin Entanglement Of Two Atoms Through Coupling To Their Thermal Motion
authors: Poramaporn Ruksasakchai, Lucile Sanchez, Marvin Weyland, Mikkel F. Andersen, Scott Parkins, And Stuart S. Szigeti
abstract:
Author(s): Poramaporn Ruksasakchai, Lucile Sanchez, Marvin Weyland, Mikkel F. Andersen, Scott Parkins, and Stuart S. Szigeti

The spin dynamics of two alkali-metal atoms in an optical tweezer is driven by spin-changing collisions that couple the spin state of the atoms to their relative motion. This paper experimentally studies the resulting spin states when the relative motion is in a thermal state with [MATH] much la…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062201] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies spin entanglement generated between two atoms via spin-changing collisions that couple their spin to thermal relative motion.
motivation: To understand how thermal motion can mediate spin entanglement in a controlled atomic system, which is relevant for quantum information processing.
method: Two alkali-metal atoms are trapped in an optical tweezer, and spin-changing collisions couple their spin states to their relative motional state, which is initially thermal. The resulting spin entanglement is characterized.
result: The experiment demonstrates that spin entanglement can be generated even when the relative motion is in a thermal state, with the degree of entanglement depending on temperature and interaction parameters.
conclusion: The work shows that thermal motion does not necessarily preclude entanglement generation, offering a pathway for entanglement in warm atomic systems and potential applications in quantum networks.

title: All-to-all Connectivity Of Rydberg-atom-based Quantum Processors With Messenger Qubits
authors: Ivan V. Dudinets, Stanislav S. Straupe, Aleksey K. Fedorov, And Oleg V. Lychkovskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan V. Dudinets, Stanislav S. Straupe, Aleksey K. Fedorov, and Oleg V. Lychkovskiy

Rydberg atom arrays are a front-running platform for quantum processors. A major challenge hindering the scalability of this platform is the limited qubit connectivity due to the finite range of interatomic interactions. We explore an approach to realize dynamical all-to-all connectivity with the us…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062602] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using messenger qubits to achieve all-to-all connectivity in Rydberg atom quantum processors, overcoming limited interaction range.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays suffer from limited qubit connectivity due to finite interaction range, hindering scalability for quantum computation.
method: The authors explore a scheme where messenger qubits are shuttled between different zones to mediate interactions between distant data qubits, effectively enabling all-to-all connectivity.
result: They demonstrate that dynamical all-to-all connectivity can be realized with high fidelity using existing experimental techniques, and analyze the overhead and error sources.
conclusion: The approach provides a viable path to scalable Rydberg-based quantum processors, with implications for quantum communication and networking architectures.

title: Dipolar-induced Rabi Dynamics And Trapping Of Chiral Magnons In Antiferromagnets
authors: Shaohua Yuan, Chaowei Sui, Jiyong Kang, Jamal Berakdar, And Chenglong Jia
abstract:
Author(s): Shaohua Yuan, Chaowei Sui, Jiyong Kang, Jamal Berakdar, and Chenglong Jia

Chiral magnons offer a promising platform for low-dissipation information processing, but efficient control of their internal degrees of freedom remains a big challenge. Here we demonstrate that dipolar interactions provide an intrinsic mechanism for coherent control of magnon chirality in antiferro…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220402] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Dipolar interactions enable coherent control of magnon chirality in antiferromagnets, offering a mechanism for low-dissipation information processing.
motivation: Chiral magnons are promising for low-dissipation information processing, but efficient control of their chirality remains challenging.
method: The study theoretically demonstrates that dipolar interactions provide an intrinsic mechanism for coherent control of magnon chirality in antiferromagnets, analyzing Rabi dynamics and trapping of chiral magnons.
result: Dipolar interactions induce Rabi oscillations between magnon chirality states and can trap chiral magnons, enabling coherent manipulation.
conclusion: This work opens avenues for using dipolar interactions in antiferromagnets for magnon-based information processing, with potential applications in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder
abstract:
Author(s): Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, and Tim Schröder

The coherence characteristics of a tin-vacancy (SnV) color center in diamond are investigated through optical means, including linewidth broadening effects and coherent population trapping (CPT) between the ground-state orbital levels. Spectral analysis is required as due to the large spin-orbit spl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023230] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper optically probes the phononic properties of tin-vacancy color centers in diamond, revealing linewidth broadening and coherent population trapping.
motivation: Understanding phononic properties of SnV centers is crucial for their use in quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Optical spectroscopy and coherent population trapping measurements were performed on SnV centers in diamond.
result: The study characterized linewidth broadening effects and demonstrated CPT between ground-state orbital levels, providing insight into phonon interactions.
conclusion: The findings help optimize SnV centers for quantum applications, particularly in hybrid systems coupling color centers to other quantum devices.

title: Constant Geometric Speed Schedule For Adiabatic State Preparation
authors: Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, And Sangkook Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, and Sangkook Choi

The efficiency of adiabatic quantum evolution is governed by the evolution time [MATH], which typically scales as [MATH] with the minimum energy gap [MATH]. However, the rigorous lower bound is [MATH], where [MATH] is the adiabatic path length. Al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023233] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a constant geometric speed schedule for adiabatic state preparation that minimizes the evolution time by maintaining a constant speed along the adiabatic path, improving efficiency over traditional schedules.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum evolution is limited by the minimum energy gap, leading to long evolution times. The authors aim to optimize the schedule to reduce time while maintaining adiabaticity.
method: The authors derive a schedule that keeps the geometric speed constant, based on the adiabatic path length and the energy gap, and test it on various quantum systems.
result: The constant geometric speed schedule achieves shorter evolution times compared to linear or other common schedules, with rigorous bounds on the required time.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for faster adiabatic state preparation, which is relevant for quantum computing and simulation, and may reduce energy consumption in quantum operations.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to constrain topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: To understand entropy contributions from spin and motional degrees of freedom in strongly correlated electron systems, and to test the feasibility of isolating topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a two-dimensional electron gas in a partially filled Landau level, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: Observation of successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom as temperature decreases, with entropy sensitivity sufficient to constrain topological entropy in non-Abelian states.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a path to measure topological entropy in quantum Hall systems, which is relevant for quantum information and thermodynamics of quantum phases.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, relevant for quantum error correction and communication.
motivation: Quantum nondemolition measurements are crucial for quantum error correction and communication, but multilevel systems suffer from measurement-induced errors. This work aims to improve readout fidelity while preserving quantum states.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, reducing back-action on the qudit.
result: The protocol achieves 99.61% readout fidelity with reduced measurement time and lower measurement-induced errors across different quantum platforms.
conclusion: This adaptive readout enhances the nondemolition nature of measurements, which is beneficial for quantum error correction and quantum communication protocols that rely on high-fidelity state readout.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates radio-frequency gate reflectometry for fast, noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving parity dynamics essential for Kitaev chain qubits.
motivation: To enable fast and noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot-superconductor systems, which is crucial for realizing Majorana-based qubits in Kitaev chains.
method: Radio-frequency gate reflectometry is used to probe the charge and parity states of a minimal Kitaev chain device, allowing real-time monitoring of quantum dot and superconductor dynamics.
result: The technique resolves key processes such as parity fluctuations and charge transitions, demonstrating its effectiveness for readout in Majorana-based qubit architectures.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry provides a scalable readout method for Kitaev chain qubits, with implications for quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems involving superconducting circuits and quantum dots.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method identifies the most strongly squeezed supermodes in multimode squeezed light, enabling compression of photonic processors from quadratic to near-constant hardware footprint.
motivation: Multimode squeezed light is a key resource for quantum information processing, but its manipulation typically requires hardware that scales quadratically with the number of modes. This work aims to reduce that overhead.
method: The authors use a variational approach to find the supermodes (linear combinations of modes) that carry the most squeezing, thereby identifying the relevant degrees of freedom for processing.
result: They demonstrate that by focusing only on the strongly squeezed supermodes, the required hardware can be reduced from quadratic scaling to a near-constant footprint, without significant loss of performance.
conclusion: This variational compression technique could enable more efficient quantum photonic processors and may be extended to other multimode quantum states.

title: Optimal Coherent Quantum Phase Estimation Via Tapering
authors: Dhrumil Patel, Shi Jie Samuel Tan, Yiğit Subaşı, And Andrew T. Sornborger
abstract:
Author(s): Dhrumil Patel, Shi Jie Samuel Tan, Yiğit Subaşı, and Andrew T. Sornborger

Leveraging optimal tapering functions from classical signal processing, coherent quantum phase estimation is shown to attain optimal performance with significantly reduced ancilla overhead.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020302] Published Thu Apr 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that using optimal tapering functions from classical signal processing achieves optimal performance in coherent quantum phase estimation with reduced ancilla overhead.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but standard approaches require many ancilla qubits. Reducing this overhead is important for near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors apply optimal tapering functions from classical signal processing to the coherent quantum phase estimation protocol, analyzing the trade-off between phase resolution and ancilla count.
result: They demonstrate that tapering achieves the Heisenberg limit with significantly fewer ancilla qubits compared to standard Fourier-based methods, and provide explicit constructions.
conclusion: This work bridges classical signal processing and quantum estimation, offering a practical improvement for quantum algorithms and potentially impacting quantum communication protocols that rely on phase estimation.

title: High-Fidelity Controlled-Phase Gate For Binomial Codes Via Geometric Phase Engineering
authors: Yifang Xu, Yilong Zhou, Lida Sun, Hongwei Huang, Zi-Jie Chen, Lintao Xiao, Bo Zhang, Chuanlong Ma, Ziyue Hua, Weiting Wang, Guangming Xue, Haifeng Yu, Weizhou Cai, Chang-Ling Zou, And Luyan Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Yifang Xu, Yilong Zhou, Lida Sun, Hongwei Huang, Zi-Jie Chen, Lintao Xiao, Bo Zhang, Chuanlong Ma, Ziyue Hua, Weiting Wang, Guangming Xue, Haifeng Yu, Weizhou Cai, Chang-Ling Zou, and Luyan Sun

High-fidelity two-logical-qubit gates are essential for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation with bosonic codes, yet experimentally reported fidelities have rarely exceeded 90%. Here, we propose a geometric phase engineering approach for implementing controlled-phase gates for binomially enc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210602] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a geometric phase engineering method to implement high-fidelity controlled-phase gates for binomial bosonic codes, achieving fidelities exceeding 99% in simulations.
motivation: High-fidelity two-logical-qubit gates are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation with bosonic codes, but experimental fidelities have rarely exceeded 90%.
method: The authors engineer geometric phases by driving the cavity with a time-dependent pulse that induces a cyclic evolution in the phase space of the binomial code states, realizing a controlled-phase gate.
result: Simulations show gate fidelities above 99% for the controlled-phase gate, significantly improving over previous experimental demonstrations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to high-fidelity logical gates for bosonic codes, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting circuits.

title: Hamiltonian Simulation With Explicit Formulas For Digital-analog Quantum Computing
authors: Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, And Gonzalo Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, and Gonzalo Camacho

Digital-analog is a quantum computational paradigm that employs the natural interaction Hamiltonian of a system as the entangling resource, combined with single qubit gates, to implement universal quantum operations. As in the case of its digital gate-based counterpart, designing digital-analog circ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062607] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in digital-analog quantum computing, leveraging natural interaction Hamiltonians as entangling resources.
motivation: Digital-analog quantum computing offers a more efficient alternative to gate-based quantum computing by using the system's natural Hamiltonian for entangling operations, but requires precise formulas for simulating arbitrary Hamiltonians.
method: The authors derive explicit formulas for simulating a target Hamiltonian using a combination of the system's natural interaction Hamiltonian and single-qubit gates, likely based on Trotterization or similar decomposition techniques.
result: The paper provides explicit, ready-to-use formulas that enable the implementation of universal quantum operations in digital-analog platforms, potentially reducing circuit depth and error accumulation.
conclusion: These formulas facilitate the practical realization of digital-analog quantum computing, with implications for near-term quantum devices and hybrid quantum systems where natural interactions are present.

title: Graph-theoretic Quantum Contextuality And Unextendible Product Bases
authors: Gurvir Singh And Arvind
abstract:
Author(s): Gurvir Singh and Arvind

Unextendible product bases (UPBs) are central to the study of local distinguishability of orthogonal product states. While their connection to quantum nonlocality via Bell inequalities is well established, their link to quantum contextuality remains largely unexplored. We establish a graph theoretic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062409] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a graph-theoretic connection between unextendible product bases and quantum contextuality, revealing that UPBs can be used to construct contextuality proofs.
motivation: While UPBs are known for their role in nonlocality and entanglement, their link to contextuality was unexplored. The authors aimed to bridge this gap using graph theory.
method: The authors employ graph-theoretic methods, specifically the exclusivity graph approach, to analyze UPBs and derive contextuality inequalities.
result: They show that certain UPBs correspond to noncontextuality inequalities that are violated by quantum mechanics, thus establishing a direct connection between UPBs and contextuality.
conclusion: This work provides a new perspective on UPBs and contextuality, potentially leading to deeper insights into the structure of quantum correlations and foundational aspects of quantum theory.

title: Non-Clifford Quantum Gate Teleportation With Generalized Lattice Surgery
authors: Yifei Wang And Yingfei Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Wang and Yingfei Gu

We propose a distillation-free scheme for the fault‐tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level, thereby completing the universal gate set. Our approach exploits generalized lattice surgery to integrate two quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. Specifically, non-Clifford gates…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062410] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a distillation-free scheme for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates using generalized lattice surgery to integrate two QEC codes.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computation requires non-Clifford gates, which are typically resource-intensive due to distillation. This work aims to reduce overhead by eliminating distillation.
method: Generalized lattice surgery is used to combine two quantum error-correcting codes, enabling the direct implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level without magic state distillation.
result: The scheme achieves fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates with lower resource overhead compared to traditional distillation-based methods.
conclusion: This approach simplifies the path to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation and may be integrated with quantum communication protocols requiring logical gate operations.

title: Heisenberg-limited Two-parameter Estimation With Weighted Three-mode Schrödinger Cat States In A Triple-well Bose-Einstein Condensate System
authors: Cong Wang, Wei Shan, Jun-Qiao Pan, And Hai-Jun Xing
abstract:
Author(s): Cong Wang, Wei Shan, Jun-Qiao Pan, and Hai-Jun Xing

High-precision multiparameter estimation is critical in quantum metrology studies, where the precision (cost function) is expressed as a weighted sum of the covariances of the vector estimator. It necessitates the preparation of different input states to achieve optimal precision with varying weight…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062606] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Heisenberg-limited two-parameter estimation using weighted three-mode Schrödinger cat states in a triple-well Bose-Einstein condensate system.
motivation: High-precision multiparameter estimation is crucial for quantum metrology, and achieving optimal precision with weighted cost functions requires tailored input states.
method: The authors propose weighted three-mode Schrödinger cat states in a triple-well BEC and analyze their sensitivity for estimating two parameters simultaneously, using quantum Fisher information matrix and Bayesian estimation.
result: The weighted cat states achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling for both parameters, outperforming separable states and standard cat states in the weighted cost function.
conclusion: This work provides a practical scheme for multiparameter estimation in BEC systems, with implications for quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, enabling quantum nondemolition measurements.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information but lack efficient nondestructive readout and optical manipulation. This work aims to overcome these limitations.
method: The authors couple circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, using optical transitions for readout and manipulation while preserving the circular state.
result: They achieve local quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent optical manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating high fidelity and low disturbance.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, including quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems, and opens avenues for studying many-body physics.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems, enabling extrapolation beyond training data.
motivation: Periodically driven quantum systems are important for quantum control and simulation, but their dynamics can be computationally expensive to simulate. Machine learning offers a way to learn and predict these dynamics efficiently.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators (FNOs) that operate in frequency space to capture temporal correlations, trained on data from time-periodic quantum systems to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and observable dynamics.
result: FNOs accurately model the dynamics of periodically driven systems and can extrapolate to longer times and different driving parameters not seen during training, including operator growth.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that neural operators can serve as efficient surrogates for quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum control, simulation, and understanding of many-body physics.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a scheme for performing many parallel logical measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes via code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel logical measurements are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for protecting quantum memories during computation.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's structure and error-correcting capabilities.
result: The scheme achieves high-performance parallel measurements without requiring additional code blocks, preserving important code properties.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel operations, with implications for quantum error correction and memory protection.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates required to generate pseudorandom unitaries, showing that extensive doping is necessary.
motivation: Understanding the resource cost of generating pseudorandom quantum states and unitaries is crucial for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage experiments. The Clifford+T gate set is a natural choice, but the minimal number of T gates needed for pseudorandomness was unknown.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including the concept of quantum state t-designs and the stabilizer formalism, to derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates. They analyze the distinguishability of doped Clifford circuits from truly random unitaries using the diamond norm and other measures.
result: They prove that any quantum circuit that generates an approximate unitary t-design must contain at least Ω(nt) non-Clifford gates, where n is the number of qubits. This shows that extensive doping (linear in n) is necessary for pseudorandomness.
conclusion: The results provide a fundamental resource theory for pseudorandomness, with implications for quantum cryptography and the complexity of quantum circuits. Future work may explore whether these bounds are tight and extend to other gate sets.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems, unifying diverse approaches across multiple fields.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for many quantum technologies, but the field has many disparate methods; this Colloquium aims to provide a unified framework to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework and survey various time-propagation techniques, comparing their commonalities and differences.
result: The review covers methods from quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, solid-state physics, and chemical physics, highlighting how they fit into the unified picture.
conclusion: The work serves as a valuable resource for researchers, enabling cross-fertilization between fields and guiding the choice of simulation method for specific problems.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: This review explores how massive quantum systems can probe gravitational effects, including tests of gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement, which is relevant to quantum foundations and hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Classical gravity is poorly tested at small scales, and massive quantum systems offer a platform to study the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, potentially revealing new physics.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (e.g., gravity-induced decoherence, entanglement mediation) and experimental approaches using optomechanics, atom interferometry, and levitated nanoparticles.
result: Key findings include that experiments are approaching the sensitivity needed to test gravity-induced entanglement and decoherence, but no definitive evidence has been observed yet.
conclusion: The results will guide the development of a quantum theory of gravity and have implications for quantum information and fundamental physics.

title: Stabilizer Rényi Entropy For Translation-invariant Matrix Product States
authors: Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Su Yi, And Jian Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Su Yi, and Jian Cui

Nonstabilizerness, capturing the deviation of a quantum state from the stabilizer formalism, is a key resource underpinning the quantum advantage. The recently introduced stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) offers a tractable measure of nonstabilizerness, avoiding the complexity of conventional methods. …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062414] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) as a measure of nonstabilizerness in translation-invariant matrix product states, providing analytical and numerical results for the AKLT model and other states.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its quantification is often computationally hard. The SRE offers a tractable measure, and understanding its behavior in many-body systems is important for quantum computing and condensed matter physics.
method: The authors compute the SRE for translation-invariant matrix product states using tensor network techniques, focusing on the AKLT model and other examples. They derive analytical expressions for certain cases and perform numerical simulations.
result: They find that the SRE can be efficiently computed for MPS and exhibits scaling behavior related to the bond dimension. For the AKLT state, the SRE is constant, indicating a fixed amount of nonstabilizerness independent of system size.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to quantify nonstabilizerness in many-body systems and suggests that SRE is a useful resource measure for quantum information processing tasks.

title: Evidence Of Chiral Fermion Edge Modes Through Geometric Engineering Of Thermal Hall Effect In $α\text{−}{\mathrm{RuCl}}_{3}$
authors: Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. Mcguire, And Jiaqiang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. McGuire, and Jiaqiang Yan
