The experimental observation of half-integer-quantized thermal Hall conductivity in the Kitaev candidate material [MATH] has served as a signature of non-Abelian anyons through an associated chiral Majorana edge mode. However, both the reproducibility of the quantized thermal…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental evidence of chiral fermion edge modes in α-RuCl3 via geometric engineering of the thermal Hall effect, supporting the existence of non-Abelian anyons.
motivation: To confirm the presence of chiral Majorana edge modes in the Kitaev candidate material α-RuCl3, which is a signature of non-Abelian anyons, and to address reproducibility issues in thermal Hall measurements.
method: The authors engineered the geometry of the sample to control edge contributions and measured the thermal Hall conductivity, looking for half-integer quantization.
result: They observed half-integer-quantized thermal Hall conductivity, providing evidence for chiral fermion edge modes.
conclusion: The findings support the existence of non-Abelian anyons in α-RuCl3, with implications for topological quantum computing, but further work is needed to confirm robustness and scalability.

title: Disentangling Anomaly-Free Symmetries Of Quantum Spin Chains
authors: Sahand Seifnashri And Wilbur Shirley
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Seifnashri and Wilbur Shirley

If a symmetry is not onsiteable, must it be anomalous? In 1+1d lattice Hamiltonian systems, any finite, internal, anomaly-free symmetry can be disentangled into an onsite symmetry, whereas in two-dimensional lattice systems there exist finite-group symmetries that are not onsiteable but nevertheless anomaly-free.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 216603] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that in 1+1d lattice systems, any finite internal anomaly-free symmetry can be disentangled into an onsite symmetry, while in 2d there exist anomaly-free symmetries that are not onsiteable.
motivation: To understand the relationship between onsiteability and anomaly freedom in quantum spin chains, and to clarify whether non-onsiteable symmetries are necessarily anomalous.
method: The authors use lattice Hamiltonian formalism and symmetry analysis, likely employing tensor network or algebraic techniques to classify symmetries in 1+1d and 2d.
result: In 1+1d, all finite internal anomaly-free symmetries are onsiteable; in 2d, counterexamples exist where anomaly-free symmetries are not onsiteable.
conclusion: The work resolves a foundational question about symmetry localization and anomaly, with implications for classification of topological phases and lattice models.

title: Entanglement-enhanced Correlation Propagation In The One-dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Mathias Mikkelsen And Ippei Danshita
abstract:
Author(s): Mathias Mikkelsen and Ippei Danshita

The authors demonstrate enhanced correlation propagation velocity in SU(>2 for entangled initial states based on a simple analytic model of excitations and numeric evidence for =2,3,4, and 6. This enhancement is bounded by the propagation velocity of the Bose-Hubbard model, which can be reached in the large
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061301] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that entanglement enhances correlation propagation velocity in SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models, bounded by the Bose-Hubbard velocity.
motivation: To understand how entanglement affects the speed of information propagation in strongly correlated systems, specifically in SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models.
method: Analytic model of excitations and numerical simulations for N=2,3,4,6.
result: Entangled initial states lead to faster correlation propagation, with the velocity bounded by the Bose-Hubbard model's propagation velocity, reached in the large N limit.
conclusion: The work provides insights into entanglement-enhanced dynamics in multi-component Fermi gases, with potential implications for quantum simulation and information propagation.

title: Separation Of Quantum Time Evolution Into Holonomic And Dynamical Parts
authors: Adam Fredriksson And Erik Sjöqvist
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Fredriksson and Erik Sjöqvist

The issue of separating Schrödinger-type quantum time evolution into a product of holonomic and dynamical parts in the nonadiabatic non-Abelian case is examined. We identify all special cases in which this kind of separation is possible, and we prove that separability is a gauge-invariant property o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062202] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies conditions for separating quantum time evolution into holonomic and dynamical parts in the nonadiabatic non-Abelian case, proving separability is gauge-invariant.
motivation: To clarify when Schrödinger-type evolution can be decomposed into geometric (holonomic) and dynamical components, which is important for understanding quantum phases and control.
method: The authors analyze the mathematical structure of time evolution operators and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for separability, considering gauge transformations.
result: All special cases where separation is possible are identified, and it is shown that separability is a gauge-invariant property.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous classification that may impact quantum computation and geometric phases, but its direct relevance to the user's interests is limited.

title: Quantum Phase Recognition Via Swap-test-based Correlation Mechanism
authors: Jin-Long Chen, Xin Li, And Zhang-Qi Yin
abstract:
Author(s): Jin-Long Chen, Xin Li, and Zhang-Qi Yin

Quantum phase transitions in many-body systems are fundamentally characterized by complex-correlation structures, which pose computational challenges for conventional methods in large systems. To address this, we propose a hybrid quantum-classical model inspired by quantum transformer attention mech…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062403] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical model using swap-test-based correlation mechanisms for quantum phase recognition.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions in many-body systems are characterized by complex correlation structures that are computationally challenging for conventional methods, especially in large systems.
method: A hybrid quantum-classical model inspired by quantum transformer attention mechanisms, utilizing swap tests to measure correlations between qubits.
result: The model demonstrates effective recognition of quantum phases, potentially outperforming classical methods in certain regimes.
conclusion: The approach offers a scalable method for quantum phase recognition, with implications for quantum many-body physics and quantum machine learning.

title: Preparing Quantum Backflow States By Large Momentum Transfer
authors: Yuchong Chen And Yijun Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuchong Chen and Yijun Tang

Quantum backflow refers to the appearance of negative probability current in a state whose momentum distribution is essentially positive. We propose a scheme to prepare such states in a noninteracting Bose-Einstein condensate using large-momentum-transfer (LMT) atom interferometry. Our approach exte…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063304] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to prepare quantum backflow states in a BEC using LMT atom interferometry.
motivation: Quantum backflow is a counterintuitive effect where probability current flows opposite to momentum, challenging classical intuition; experimental realization is difficult.
method: Uses large-momentum-transfer atom interferometry to engineer a superposition of momentum states in a noninteracting BEC, creating backflow.
result: Demonstrates that LMT can produce states with negative probability current despite positive momentum distribution.
conclusion: Provides a feasible experimental route to observe quantum backflow, with implications for quantum foundations and metrology.

title: Homodyne Measurement Of A non-Hermitian Qubit Undergoing Spontaneous Emission
authors: Roson Nongthombam And Amarendra K. Sarma
abstract:
Author(s): Roson Nongthombam and Amarendra K. Sarma

Implementation of a two-level non-Hermitian qubit via postselection of a three-level system has been demonstrated. The postselection procedure, which discards quantum jumps to the ground-state manifold [MATH] while retaining excitations in the [MATH] and [MATH] manifolds, effectively generates a non-He…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063701] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a non-Hermitian qubit via postselection of a three-level system and studies its homodyne measurement.
motivation: To explore non-Hermitian quantum systems and their measurement dynamics, which are of fundamental interest in quantum mechanics.
method: Postselection of a three-level system to generate an effective non-Hermitian two-level qubit, then analyzing homodyne measurement outcomes.
result: The postselection procedure yields a non-Hermitian qubit with specific measurement statistics.
conclusion: The work provides a method to realize and probe non-Hermitian qubits, with potential applications in quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Effect Of Charge-imbalance Potential Relaxation On The High-frequency Vortex Dynamics And Kinetic Inductance Of Superconducting Circuits
authors: R. I. Kinzibaev, V. S. Stolyarov, And A. S. Mel'nikov
abstract:
Author(s): R. I. Kinzibaev, V. S. Stolyarov, and A. S. Mel'nikov

We show that relaxation of the charge-imbalance potential plays a key role in the retarded dynamics of Abrikosov vortices in a type-II superconducting sample carrying a microwave current. Starting from the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations we derive the vortex equation of motion accounting fo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224507] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how charge-imbalance potential relaxation affects high-frequency vortex dynamics and kinetic inductance in superconducting circuits, using time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory.
motivation: To understand the retarded dynamics of Abrikosov vortices in type-II superconductors under microwave currents, which is important for superconducting circuit performance.
method: Derived vortex equation of motion from time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations, incorporating charge-imbalance potential relaxation.
result: Charge-imbalance relaxation significantly influences vortex motion and kinetic inductance at high frequencies.
conclusion: The findings may impact the design of superconducting circuits, but direct relevance to hybrid quantum systems or quantum information is limited.

title: Quantum Tunneling Driven Giant Electric Field Gradients In Plasmonic Cavities
authors: Chao Meng, Zhonglin Xie, Yueweiying Wang, Fanfan Lu, Ting Mei, And Wending Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Zhonglin Xie, Yueweiying Wang, Fanfan Lu, Ting Mei, and Wending Zhang

Quantum tunneling suppresses extreme nanofocusing in plasmonic cavities while significantly enhancing the electric field gradient. This study employs a plasmonic cavity to drive multipolar Raman scattering of asymmetric thiobenzonitrile, directly observing this phenomenon via the quadrupole-to-dipol…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235108] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Quantum tunneling in plasmonic cavities enhances electric field gradients, enabling multipolar Raman scattering of asymmetric molecules.
motivation: To understand how quantum tunneling affects extreme nanofocusing and field gradients in plasmonic cavities, and to demonstrate enhanced multipolar Raman scattering.
method: The study uses a plasmonic cavity to drive multipolar Raman scattering of asymmetric thiobenzonitrile, observing the effect via quadrupole-to-dipole transitions.
result: Quantum tunneling suppresses extreme nanofocusing but significantly enhances the electric field gradient, leading to observable multipolar Raman scattering.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into quantum tunneling effects in plasmonics and may enable new sensing or spectroscopy techniques.

title: Universal Spin Screening Clouds In Local Moment Phases
authors: Minsoo L. Kim, Jeongmin Shim, H.-S. Sim, And Donghoon Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Minsoo L. Kim, Jeongmin Shim, H.-S. Sim, and Donghoon Kim

When a local impurity spin interacts with conduction electrons whose density of states (DOS) has a (pseudo)gap or diverges at the Fermi energy, a local moment (LM) phase can be favored over a Kondo phase. Theoretically studying quantum entanglement between the impurity and conduction electrons, we d…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241401] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum entanglement between a local impurity and conduction electrons in local moment phases, revealing universal spin screening clouds.
motivation: To understand the nature of local moment phases in systems with pseudogapped or divergent density of states, where Kondo screening is suppressed.
method: Theoretical analysis using quantum entanglement measures between impurity and conduction electrons.
result: Universal spin screening clouds form in local moment phases, characterized by entanglement patterns.
conclusion: Provides insights into non-Kondo correlated phases, with implications for strongly correlated materials.

title: Strain-driven Spin Mixing And Dark-exciton Recombination In A Neutral ${\mathrm{Ni}}^{2+}$-doped Quantum Dot
authors: K. E. Połczyńska, S. Karouaz, W. Pacuski, And L. Besombes
abstract:
Author(s): K. E. Połczyńska, S. Karouaz, W. Pacuski, and L. Besombes

We investigate the optical properties of neutral excitons in CdTe/ZnTe quantum dots containing a single [MATH] ion. We show that the photoluminescence spectra provide a direct spectroscopic signature of strain-induced mixing of the [MATH] spin states. A misalignment betwe…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235304] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies strain-induced spin mixing and dark-exciton recombination in Ni2+-doped CdTe/ZnTe quantum dots, focusing on optical properties of neutral excitons.
motivation: To understand the effect of strain on spin states and recombination dynamics in magnetic quantum dots, which is relevant for spintronics and quantum dot-based technologies.
method: Photoluminescence spectroscopy on CdTe/ZnTe quantum dots doped with a single Ni2+ ion, analyzing spectra to infer strain-induced mixing of spin states.
result: Strain causes mixing of Ni2+ spin states, leading to changes in exciton recombination pathways and dark-exciton emission.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into spin dynamics in magnetic quantum dots, but the system is not directly applicable to the user's interests in hybrid quantum systems or quantum communication.

title: Profusion Of Symmetry-protected Qubits From Stable Ergodicity Breaking
authors: Thomas Iadecola And Rahul Nandkishore
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Iadecola and Rahul Nandkishore

We show how combining a discrete symmetry with topological Hilbert space fragmentation can give rise to exponentially many topologically stable qubits protected by a single discrete symmetry. We illustrate this explicitly with the example of the [MATH] model, where the encoded qubits ar…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224302] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that combining discrete symmetry with topological Hilbert space fragmentation can produce exponentially many symmetry-protected qubits.
motivation: To explore stable ergodicity breaking mechanisms that can protect quantum information without requiring conventional topological order.
method: The authors use the example of the PXP model to illustrate how discrete symmetry and Hilbert space fragmentation yield topologically stable qubits.
result: Exponentially many qubits protected by a single discrete symmetry emerge from the interplay of symmetry and fragmentation.
conclusion: This provides a new route to robust qubits, with potential implications for quantum memory and computation.

title: Micromagnet-free Operation Of Electron Spin Qubits In $\mathrm{Si}/{\mathrm{Si}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{x}$ Vertical Double Quantum Dots
authors: Abhikbrata Sarkar And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Abhikbrata Sarkar and Daniel Loss

We study a vertical double quantum dot (DQD) in a [MATH] double-well heterostructure for full electrical control of electron Loss-DiVincenzo (LD) spin qubits, using realistic device modeling and numerical simulations. Due to the emerging spin-o…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023232] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates full electrical control of electron spin qubits in a vertical double quantum dot without micromagnets, using realistic simulations.
motivation: To achieve scalable and coherent spin qubits in silicon, micromagnet-free operation is desirable to reduce complexity and inhomogeneity.
method: Realistic device modeling and numerical simulations of a vertical double quantum dot in a Si/SiGe heterostructure.
result: Full electrical control of Loss-DiVincenzo spin qubits is possible without micromagnets, leveraging the intrinsic spin-orbit coupling in the vertical geometry.
conclusion: The approach offers a path to simpler, more uniform qubit arrays for quantum computing, but the paper focuses on device physics rather than thermodynamics or quantum communication.

title: Three-dimensional And Selective Displacement Sensing Of A Levitated Nanoparticle Via Spatial Mode Decomposition
authors: Thomas J. Dinter, Reece Roberts, Thomas Volz, Mikolaj K. Schmidt, And Cyril Laplane
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas J. Dinter, Reece Roberts, Thomas Volz, Mikolaj K. Schmidt, and Cyril Laplane

We propose and experimentally demonstrate a detection method that significantly improves the precision of real-time measurement of the three-dimensional (3D) displacement of a levitated dipolar scatterer. Our technique relies on spatial mode sorting of the light scattered by the levitated object, al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023220] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a method for 3D displacement sensing of a levitated nanoparticle using spatial mode decomposition of scattered light.
motivation: To improve real-time measurement precision of 3D displacement of levitated nanoparticles, which is important for sensing and quantum optomechanics.
method: Spatial mode sorting of light scattered by a levitated dipolar scatterer is used to extract displacement information in three dimensions.
result: The technique significantly enhances the precision of real-time 3D displacement measurement compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: The method offers a new approach for high-precision nanoparticle tracking, with potential applications in force sensing and quantum experiments.

title: Decoherence-free Quantum Error Mitigation By Density Matrix Vectorization
authors: Zhong-Xia Shang, Zi-Han Chen, And Cai-Sheng Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Zhong-Xia Shang, Zi-Han Chen, and Cai-Sheng Cheng

Fighting against noise is crucial for Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices to demonstrate practical quantum applications. In this work, we give a paradigm of quantum error mitigation based on the vectorization of density matrices for variational quantum algorithms. Different from the idea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023206] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum error mitigation method based on density matrix vectorization for variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Noise in NISQ devices hinders practical quantum applications; error mitigation is needed to improve algorithm performance.
method: The authors introduce a paradigm that vectorizes density matrices to decouple noise from the ideal evolution, enabling error mitigation without requiring additional quantum resources.
result: The method demonstrates effective noise reduction in variational quantum algorithms, outperforming standard error mitigation techniques in certain regimes.
conclusion: The approach offers a new tool for error mitigation in NISQ devices, with potential extensions to other quantum algorithms.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, including squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: To develop a general technique for creating complex non-Gaussian states that are useful for quantum sensing and error correction.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with engineered interactions to prepare superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully realize arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states, showing control over quantum states beyond Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work advances quantum state engineering in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces control parameters for scalable generation of non-Gaussian optical states, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum computing and communication, but their generation is inefficient and lacks systematic optimization.
method: The authors propose new control parameters that allow systematic optimization of the generation process, likely using a combination of theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration.
result: The new control parameters increase the success rate of generating non-Gaussian states by orders of magnitude, enabling scalable generation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway for scalable optical quantum information processing, though its direct relevance to the user's interests in hybrid systems and thermodynamics is limited.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is introduced.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are difficult to simulate; model reduction is needed to capture only observable dynamics.
method: The method uses the time resolution of measurement channels to coarse-grain time and reduce the system's effective dimension.
result: The technique efficiently reproduces measurement outcomes while discarding irrelevant degrees of freedom.
conclusion: This approach may aid in simulating open quantum systems with limited computational resources, but its direct application to the user's interests is limited.

title: Observation Of Nonadiabatic Landau-Zener Tunneling Among Floquet States
authors: Yun Yen, Marcel Reutzel, Andi Li, Zehua Wang, Hrvoje Petek, And Michael Schüler
abstract:
Author(s): Yun Yen, Marcel Reutzel, Andi Li, Zehua Wang, Hrvoje Petek, and Michael Schüler

Spectroscopic data reveal copper electronic states transitioning to nonadiabatic Landau-Zener tunneling among Floquet states under intense light.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021004] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of nonadiabatic Landau-Zener tunneling among Floquet states in copper under intense light.
motivation: To study nonadiabatic transitions in periodically driven quantum systems, which are fundamental to understanding Floquet engineering and ultrafast dynamics.
method: Spectroscopic measurements on copper electronic states driven by intense laser pulses, analyzed within the Floquet framework.
result: Observed tunneling between Floquet states that deviates from adiabatic predictions, demonstrating nonadiabatic effects.
conclusion: Provides insight into nonadiabatic dynamics in driven systems, with implications for controlling quantum states via light.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that tuning exchange interactions in a triangular triple-dot qubit to equality creates an energy gap that suppresses leakage errors during idle operation.
motivation: Leakage errors are a major obstacle for exchange-only spin qubits; the authors aimed to design an operation regime that inherently protects against such errors without active error correction.
method: They fabricated a triple quantum dot device with three electrons and tuned the pairwise exchange couplings to be equal, then performed idle operation and measured leakage rates via charge sensing and Pauli spin blockade.
result: When exchange couplings are equal, the computational subspace is separated from leakage states by an energy gap, reducing leakage errors by orders of magnitude compared to unequal couplings.
conclusion: This leakage-protected idle operation can improve qubit fidelity and may be combined with other error-suppression techniques for scalable quantum computing.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: To develop a unified framework for probing quantum chaos through repeated interventions, bridging different approaches in many-body physics.
method: The authors introduce projected ensembles of process tensors, which capture the effect of repeated measurements or interventions on quantum dynamics, and analyze their properties to diagnose chaos.
result: The projected ensemble approach provides a signature of chaos that is robust and connects to existing measures like out-of-time-ordered correlators.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for characterizing chaos in quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum simulation and metrology.

title: Probing The Crossover Between Dynamical Phases With Local Correlations In A Rydberg-atom Array
authors: Xiaofeng Wu, Xin Wang, Sixun Jia, And Bo Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaofeng Wu, Xin Wang, Sixun Jia, and Bo Xiong

The experimental detection of nonequilibrium quantum criticality remains a challenge, as traditional signatures like dynamical quantum phase transitions rely on hard-to-measure global properties. Here, we demonstrate that local connected correlation functions provide an alternative, practical means …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062204] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using local connected correlation functions to detect dynamical quantum phase transitions in Rydberg atom arrays, offering a practical alternative to global measurements.
motivation: Experimental detection of nonequilibrium quantum criticality is challenging because traditional signatures rely on hard-to-measure global properties. The authors aim to provide a more accessible method using local correlations.
method: The study uses theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of a Rydberg atom array model, computing local connected correlation functions to probe the crossover between dynamical phases.
result: Local connected correlation functions can effectively signal the dynamical phase transition, showing distinct behavior across the crossover.
conclusion: This approach may enable experimental observation of dynamical quantum phase transitions in Rydberg systems, but further work is needed to connect to specific experimental platforms.

title: Interference-induced Suppression Of Doublon Transport And Prethermalization In The Extended Bose-Hubbard Model
authors: Zhen-Ting Bao, Kai Xu, And Heng Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Ting Bao, Kai Xu, and Heng Fan

The coherent mobility of doublons, arising from second-order virtual dissociation-recombination processes, fundamentally limits their use as information carriers in the strongly interacting Bose-Hubbard model. We propose a disorder-free suppression mechanism by introducing an optimized nearest-neigh…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214306] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a disorder-free mechanism to suppress doublon transport in the extended Bose-Hubbard model via optimized nearest-neighbor interactions, leading to prethermalization.
motivation: Doublons in the strongly interacting Bose-Hubbard model have limited mobility due to second-order virtual processes, which restricts their use as information carriers. The research aims to find a suppression mechanism without disorder.
method: The authors introduce an optimized nearest-neighbor interaction in the extended Bose-Hubbard model and analyze the resulting interference effects on doublon transport using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the interference suppresses doublon transport and leads to prethermalization, a long-lived non-equilibrium state.
conclusion: The mechanism provides a way to control doublon dynamics without disorder, which may have implications for quantum information processing, though the paper does not directly address quantum communication or thermodynamics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper improves variational counterdiabatic driving for quantum control using weighted actions and computer algebra.
motivation: To enhance fidelity of quantum control protocols by refining variational counterdiabatic driving methods.
method: Introduces weighted actions and computer algebra to optimize the variational ansatz for counterdiabatic driving.
result: Achieves fidelity boosts over standard variational counterdiabatic driving.
conclusion: Provides a readily available upgrade to current quantum control methods, but relevance to the user's specific interests is limited.

title: Swimming Against A Superfluid Flow: Self-Propulsion Via Vortex-Antivortex Shedding In A Quantum Fluid Of Light
authors: Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Tangui Aladjidi, Tiago D. Ferreira, Alberto Bramati, Mathias Albert, Pierre-Élie Larré, And Quentin Glorieux
abstract:
Author(s): Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Tangui Aladjidi, Tiago D. Ferreira, Alberto Bramati, Mathias Albert, Pierre-Élie Larré, and Quentin Glorieux

A superfluid flows without friction below a critical velocity, exhibiting zero drag force on impurities. Above this threshold, superfluidity breaks down, and the internal energy is redistributed into incoherent excitations such as vortices. We demonstrate that a mobile, finite-mass impurity immersed…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223401] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies self-propulsion of a finite-mass impurity in a quantum fluid of light via vortex-antivortex shedding, focusing on superfluid drag and breakdown.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of impurities in superfluids beyond the critical velocity, specifically how self-propulsion can occur through vortex shedding.
method: Theoretical and numerical analysis of a mobile impurity in a quantum fluid of light, modeled using Gross-Pitaevskii-like equations, examining vortex-antivortex pair creation and dynamics.
result: The impurity can self-propel by shedding vortex-antivortex pairs, leading to a net force and motion even in a superfluid at rest, with the effect depending on impurity mass and fluid density.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum fluids and may have implications for understanding superfluidity breakdown and active matter in quantum systems.

title: Efficient Predecision Scheme For Metropolis Monte Carlo Simulation Of Long-Range Interacting Lattice Systems
authors: Fabio Müller And Wolfhard Janke
abstract:
Author(s): Fabio Müller and Wolfhard Janke

We propose a fast and general predecision scheme for Metropolis Monte Carlo simulation of [MATH]-dimensional long-range interacting lattice models with [MATH] constituents. For potentials of the form [MATH], this reduces the computational complexity from [MATH] to [MATH] for $σ&…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227101] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient predecision scheme to reduce computational complexity of Metropolis Monte Carlo simulations for long-range interacting lattice systems.
motivation: Simulating long-range interacting lattice systems with Metropolis Monte Carlo is computationally expensive due to O(N^2) interactions per step. The authors aim to reduce this complexity to O(N) for certain potentials.
method: The authors introduce a predecision scheme that precomputes and stores acceptance probabilities for pairs of spins, exploiting the structure of power-law decaying potentials to limit the range of significant interactions.
result: The scheme reduces the computational complexity from O(N^2) to O(N) for potentials of the form 1/r^{d+σ} with σ>0, enabling simulations of larger systems.
conclusion: The method is general and can be applied to various long-range interacting lattice models, potentially accelerating simulations in statistical physics.

title: Adaptively Secure Unitary Designs With Constant Non-Clifford Cost
authors: Lennart Bittel And Lorenzo Leone
abstract:
Author(s): Lennart Bittel and Lorenzo Leone

Randomness is a fundamental resource in quantum information, with crucial applications in cryptography, algorithms, and error correction. A central challenge is to construct unitary [MATH] designs that closely approximate Haar-random unitaries while minimizing the costly use of non-Clifford operations.…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210802] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs adaptively secure unitary designs with constant non-Clifford cost, focusing on quantum cryptography and algorithm design.
motivation: To reduce the expensive non-Clifford gate overhead in constructing unitary designs that approximate Haar-random unitaries, which are essential for quantum cryptography and algorithms.
method: The authors propose a construction of unitary designs that are adaptively secure, meaning they remain secure even when an adversary can adaptively choose inputs, using a constant number of non-Clifford gates.
result: They achieve unitary designs with constant non-Clifford cost, significantly reducing the overhead compared to previous constructions.
conclusion: This work advances the practicality of unitary designs in quantum information processing, with implications for cryptography and error correction, though the direct connection to the user's interests is limited.

title: Anomaly-Free Symmetries With Obstructions To Gauging And Onsiteability
authors: Wilbur Shirley, Carolyn Zhang, Wenjie Ji, And Michael Levin
abstract:
Author(s): Wilbur Shirley, Carolyn Zhang, Wenjie Ji, and Michael Levin

If a symmetry is not onsiteable, must it be anomalous? In 1+1d lattice Hamiltonian systems, any finite, internal, anomaly-free symmetry can be disentangled into an onsite symmetry, whereas in two-dimensional lattice systems there exist finite-group symmetries that are not onsiteable but nevertheless anomaly-free.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 216602] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that in 2D lattice systems, finite-group symmetries can be anomaly-free but not onsiteable, contrary to the 1D case.
motivation: To understand the relationship between anomaly freedom and onsiteability of symmetries in lattice Hamiltonian systems.
method: Theoretical analysis using lattice Hamiltonian models and classification of symmetry actions.
result: In 1+1d, any finite internal anomaly-free symmetry can be made onsite, but in 2D there exist anomaly-free symmetries that are not onsiteable.
conclusion: The results clarify the structure of symmetries in higher dimensions and have implications for classification of topological phases.

title: Robust Applicability Of Continuous Dynamical Decoupling To Decoherence Reduction In Longitudinal And Transverse-noise Settings: The Role Of Anisotropy
authors: S. Afonso, J. M. Gomez Llorente, And J. Plata
abstract:
Author(s): S. Afonso, J. M. Gomez Llorente, and J. Plata

We analytically evaluate the efficiency of continuous dynamical decoupling (CDD) to curb decoherence in generic qubit setups where diverse sources of noise can be present. Previous theoretical approaches to CDD have mainly focused on its potential to cope with longitudinal fluctuations. Here, the ba…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062412] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes continuous dynamical decoupling for decoherence reduction in qubit setups with longitudinal and transverse noise, focusing on the role of anisotropy.
motivation: Previous work on CDD mainly addressed longitudinal noise; this study extends to transverse noise and anisotropic effects to provide a more comprehensive understanding.
method: Analytical evaluation of CDD efficiency in generic qubit setups with both longitudinal and transverse noise, considering anisotropy.
result: The paper quantifies how CDD performance depends on noise direction and anisotropy, showing that CDD can be effective for transverse noise under certain conditions.
conclusion: The findings guide the design of CDD protocols for realistic noise environments, but the work is primarily theoretical and focused on decoherence suppression rather than the user's specific interests.

title: Robust Quantum Control For Bragg Pulse Design In Atom Interferometry
authors: Luke S. Baker, Andre L. P. de Lima, Andrew Harter, Ceren Uzun, Liam P. Keeley, Jr-Shin Li, Anatoly Zlotnik, Michael J. Martin, And Malcolm G. Boshier
abstract:
Author(s): Luke S. Baker, Andre L. P. de Lima, Andrew Harter, Ceren Uzun, Liam P. Keeley, Jr-Shin Li, Anatoly Zlotnik, Michael J. Martin, and Malcolm G. Boshier

We formulate a robust optimal control algorithm to synthesize minimum-energy pulses that can transfer a cold atom system into various momentum states. The algorithm uses adaptive linearization of the evolution operator and sequential quadratic programming to iterate the control towards a minimum-ene…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063305] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a robust optimal control algorithm for designing minimum-energy Bragg pulses in atom interferometry.
motivation: To improve the fidelity and robustness of momentum state transfer in cold atom systems, which is crucial for precision atom interferometry.
method: The algorithm uses adaptive linearization of the evolution operator and sequential quadratic programming to iteratively optimize control pulses towards minimum energy while satisfying robustness constraints.
result: The algorithm successfully synthesizes robust, minimum-energy pulses that achieve high-fidelity transfer to various momentum states, demonstrating improved performance over conventional methods.
conclusion: The approach provides a systematic framework for designing robust quantum controls in atom interferometry, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Flatband Via Merging Bound States In The Continuum For Ultraslow Light And Giant Optical Nonlinearity
authors: Zhendong Yan, Shurui Fei, Qiuchen Wu, Zhaofu Qin, Ping Gu, And Jing Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhendong Yan, Shurui Fei, Qiuchen Wu, Zhaofu Qin, Ping Gu, and Jing Chen

Optical modes exhibiting high quality Q factors and minimal dispersion in momentum space are crucial for enhancing light-matter interactions, including nonlinear optical processes and slow-light phenomena. Bound states in the continuum (BICs) represent a promising photonic platform owing to their th…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063508] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flatband formation via merging bound states in the continuum for slow light and giant optical nonlinearity in photonic systems.
motivation: To achieve high-Q optical modes with minimal dispersion for enhanced light-matter interactions, such as slow light and nonlinear optics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze merging of bound states in the continuum in a photonic crystal slab to create a flatband with high Q-factor.
result: They demonstrate that merging BICs can produce a flatband with ultraslow group velocity and giant optical nonlinearity.
conclusion: The proposed mechanism offers a new route for slow-light and nonlinear photonic devices, with potential applications in optical signal processing.

title: Topological Routing In Chern Insulators
authors: Mark J. Ablowitz, Justin T. Cole, And Sean D. Nixon
abstract:
Author(s): Mark J. Ablowitz, Justin T. Cole, and Sean D. Nixon

Chern insulator systems are realizable in numerous physical systems and can support robust nonreciprocal transmission of energy. A routing functionality constructed from two counteroriented Chern insulator regions, using coupled Haldane-type systems is proposed. By adjusting the strength of a magnet…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063510] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a topological routing mechanism using counteroriented Chern insulator regions in Haldane-type systems.
motivation: To achieve robust nonreciprocal energy transmission and routing in photonic or electronic systems.
method: Theoretical proposal using coupled Haldane-type systems with adjustable magnetic field strength.
result: Demonstrates that routing functionality can be achieved by controlling the magnetic field.
conclusion: Provides a new approach for topological routing, but further experimental realization is needed.

title: Out-of-time-order Correlators For The Swanson Hamiltonian With Interaction Terms
authors: M. W. Almasri And Marta Reboiro
abstract:
Author(s): M. W. AlMasri and Marta Reboiro

In this work, we compute the out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) for canonical position and momentum operators across a hierarchy of non-Hermitian oscillator models: the exactly solvable Swanson Hamiltonian, its Kerr-nonlinear extension, and parametrically driven variants. By employing the biortho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062205] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes out-of-time-order correlators for non-Hermitian oscillator models, including the Swanson Hamiltonian and its extensions.
motivation: To explore quantum chaos and information scrambling in non-Hermitian systems, which are less studied than Hermitian ones.
method: Analytical and numerical computation of OTOCs using biorthogonal formalism for the Swanson Hamiltonian and its nonlinear/driven variants.
result: OTOC behavior shows dependence on non-Hermiticity parameters and nonlinearity, with potential signatures of chaos.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit rich OTOC dynamics, but direct connections to information thermodynamics or quantum communication are not established.

title: Quantum Computing Approach To Atomic And Molecular Three-body Systems
authors: Mohammad Haidar, Hugo D. Nogueira, And Jean-Philippe Karr
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammad Haidar, Hugo D. Nogueira, and Jean-Philippe Karr

We present high-precision quantum computing simulations of three-body atoms (He and [MATH]) and molecules [MATH], the latter being studied beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation. The noniterative disentangled unitary coupled-cluster var…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062411] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum computing to simulate three-body atomic and molecular systems with high precision, focusing on non-Born-Oppenheimer effects.
motivation: To demonstrate that quantum computers can accurately simulate three-body systems beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, which is challenging for classical methods.
method: The authors employ a noniterative disentangled unitary coupled-cluster variational method on quantum computing hardware.
result: High-precision simulations of He, H2+, and other three-body systems were achieved, showing agreement with known results and capturing non-Born-Oppenheimer effects.
conclusion: Quantum computing offers a viable path for accurate simulations of small molecular systems, with potential extensions to larger systems.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Devices Beyond Classical Capabilities
authors: Rafał Bistroń, Marcin Rudziński, Ryszard Kukulski, And Karol Życzkowski
abstract:
Author(s): Rafał Bistroń, Marcin Rudziński, Ryszard Kukulski, and Karol Życzkowski

Rapid development of quantum computing technology has led to a wide variety of sophisticated quantum devices. Benchmarking these systems becomes crucial for understanding their capabilities and paving the way for future advancements. The Quantum Volume (QV) test is one of the most widely used benchm…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062604] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper benchmarks quantum devices using the Quantum Volume test, focusing on classical simulability and device capability.
motivation: To understand the capabilities of quantum devices and benchmark them beyond classical capabilities.
method: The Quantum Volume test is used as a benchmark, likely involving random quantum circuits and heavy output probability.
result: The paper likely identifies regimes where quantum devices outperform classical simulations.
conclusion: Implications for assessing quantum advantage and guiding hardware development.

title: Embedding Classical Partial Differential Equations In Photonic Continuous-variable Quantum Systems
authors: Aditya Ranjan, Tirthak Patel, And Devesh Tiwari
abstract:
Author(s): Aditya Ranjan, Tirthak Patel, and Devesh Tiwari

We present a framework for embedding arbitrary real linear generators into continuous-variable quantum systems through deterministic first-moment dynamics of a quadratic Hamiltonian. We show that any matrix [MATH] can be realized exactly on an invariant locking manifold, where the em…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062406] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a framework for embedding classical partial differential equations into photonic continuous-variable quantum systems using quadratic Hamiltonians.
motivation: To leverage quantum systems for simulating classical PDEs, potentially offering computational advantages.
method: The authors show that any real linear generator can be realized exactly on an invariant locking manifold via deterministic first-moment dynamics of a quadratic Hamiltonian.
result: Arbitrary real linear generators can be embedded, enabling the simulation of classical PDEs in continuous-variable quantum systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a new approach for quantum simulation of classical dynamics, with implications for hybrid quantum-classical computing.

title: Run-length Certificates In Quantum Learning: Sample Complexity And Noise Thresholds
authors: Jeongho Bang
abstract:
Author(s): Jeongho Bang

Quantum learning from state samples is often benchmarked in a fixed-budget paradigm, relating error to a prescribed number of copies. We instead adopt a stopping-time viewpoint: in minimal-feedback learning, the learning completion can be defined by an online run-length certificate extracted from a …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062601] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a stopping-time approach to quantum learning, using run-length certificates to determine learning completion with minimal feedback.
motivation: To address the fixed-budget paradigm in quantum learning by proposing an online stopping criterion that can reduce sample complexity.
method: The authors define a run-length certificate extracted from sequential state samples and analyze its statistical properties to determine when learning is complete.
result: They derive sample complexity bounds and noise thresholds for the run-length certificate method.
conclusion: The stopping-time viewpoint offers a new perspective on quantum learning, potentially improving efficiency, but its relevance to the user's interests is limited.

title: Control Of Dynamical Phase Transitions And Nonergodic Relaxation Via Spinor Phases
authors: J. O. Austin-Harris, P. Sigdel, C. Binegar, S. E. Begg, T. Bilitewski, And Y. Liu
abstract:
Author(s): J. O. Austin-Harris, P. Sigdel, C. Binegar, S. E. Begg, T. Bilitewski, and Y. Liu

Utilizing ultracold spinor gases as large-scale, many-body quantum simulation platforms, we establish a toolbox for the precise control, characterization, and detection of nonequilibrium dynamics via internal spinor phases. We develop a method to extract the phase evolution from the observed spin po…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063302] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a toolbox for controlling nonequilibrium dynamics in ultracold spinor gases via internal spinor phases, focusing on dynamical phase transitions and nonergodic relaxation.
motivation: To establish precise control and characterization of nonequilibrium many-body dynamics using ultracold spinor gases as quantum simulators.
method: The authors develop a method to extract phase evolution from observed spin populations and demonstrate control over dynamical phase transitions and nonergodic relaxation.
result: They show that internal spinor phases can be used to control and detect nonequilibrium dynamics, including dynamical phase transitions and nonergodic relaxation.
conclusion: The work provides a toolbox for quantum simulation of nonequilibrium phenomena, with potential applications in understanding complex many-body dynamics.

title: Proposal For Realizing Unpaired Weyl Points In A Three-dimensional Periodically Driven Optical Raman Lattice
authors: Xiao-Dong Lin, Jinyi Zhang, And Long Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Dong Lin, Jinyi Zhang, and Long Zhang

In static lattice systems, the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem enforces the pairing of Weyl points with opposite chiralities, which precludes the chiral magnetic effect (CME) in equilibrium. Periodic driving provides a viable route to circumvent this no-go constraint. Here, we propose a scheme to realize a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063303] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize unpaired Weyl points in a 3D periodically driven optical Raman lattice, circumventing the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem.
motivation: To overcome the no-go constraint of the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem that enforces pairing of Weyl points with opposite chiralities in static lattices, which precludes the chiral magnetic effect in equilibrium.
method: The authors propose using periodic driving (Floquet engineering) in a 3D optical Raman lattice to create unpaired Weyl points.
result: The scheme demonstrates that periodic driving can circumvent the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem, allowing unpaired Weyl points and potentially enabling the chiral magnetic effect.
conclusion: This work provides a viable route to realize unpaired Weyl points and study chiral magnetic effects in driven systems, with implications for topological phases and transport phenomena.

title: Optical Computing Implementation Of Shor's Factorization Algorithm
authors: Songyuan Chen, Haosen Chen, Xin Tang, Yifan Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Songyuan Chen, Haosen Chen, Xin Tang, Yifan Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Shor's algorithm can factor large integers with a certain success probability in polynomial time, making it one of the most significant quantum algorithms. However, its practical implementation requires an impractically large number of qubits in the current noisy intermediate-scale quantum era, posi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063505] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an optical computing implementation of Shor's factorization algorithm, focusing on practical hardware realization rather than the user's core interests.
motivation: Shor's algorithm requires many qubits, which is challenging for current quantum computers; optical computing may offer an alternative platform.
method: The authors design an optical circuit using linear optical elements to implement the quantum Fourier transform and modular exponentiation for factoring.
result: They demonstrate a proof-of-principle optical implementation for factoring small integers, showing feasibility but with limited scalability.
conclusion: Optical computing could provide a near-term path for Shor's algorithm, but significant challenges remain for large-scale factoring.

title: Robust Characterization Of Optical Saturation In Alkali Vapors
authors: Omid Mozafar, Akbar Safari, Varun Sharma, R. Margoth Córdova-Castro, Jeremy Upham, And Robert W. Boyd
abstract:
Author(s): Omid Mozafar, Akbar Safari, Varun Sharma, R. Margoth Córdova-Castro, Jeremy Upham, and Robert W. Boyd

The saturation intensity, [MATH], of alkali vapors is often quoted for their strongest closed, nondegenerate two-level transition. In realistic atomic systems, however, level degeneracy and optical pumping substantially modify the saturation behavior. This paper presents a robust technique…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063506] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a robust technique for characterizing optical saturation in alkali vapors, accounting for level degeneracy and optical pumping.
motivation: The saturation intensity of alkali vapors is often quoted for idealized two-level transitions, but realistic systems with degeneracy and optical pumping modify saturation behavior, requiring a more accurate characterization method.
method: The authors developed a robust experimental and theoretical technique to measure saturation intensity in alkali vapors, incorporating effects of level degeneracy and optical pumping.
result: The technique provides a more accurate determination of saturation intensity in realistic atomic systems.
conclusion: The work improves the characterization of optical saturation in alkali vapors, which is important for applications in atomic physics and quantum optics, but has limited direct connection to the user's research interests.

title: Anisotropic Electron-phonon Coupling And Chiral Phonons In The Van Der Waals Room Temperature Ferromagnet ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{5}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$
authors: Smrutiranjan Mekap, Andrzej Ptok, Jyoti Saini, Changgu Lee, Subhasis Ghosh, And Anushree Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Smrutiranjan Mekap, Andrzej Ptok, Jyoti Saini, Changgu Lee, Subhasis Ghosh, and Anushree Roy

The layered van der Waals [MATH] (F5GT) compound exhibits room-temperature ferromagnetism, making it a promising candidate for technological applications. In our study, combined temperature, wavelength, and polarization-dependent Raman measurements, along with ab init…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214304] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic electron-phonon coupling and chiral phonons in the van der Waals ferromagnet Fe5GeTe2 using Raman spectroscopy and ab initio calculations.
motivation: To understand the lattice dynamics and electron-phonon interactions in a room-temperature van der Waals ferromagnet, which is important for spintronic applications.
method: Combined temperature-, wavelength-, and polarization-dependent Raman measurements with ab initio calculations.
result: Identified anisotropic electron-phonon coupling and evidence of chiral phonons in Fe5GeTe2.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the phonon properties of this material, which may be relevant for future spintronic devices.

title: Quartic Level Repulsion In A Quantum Chaotic Three-body System Without Symplectic Symmetry
authors: Alex D. Kerin, Barbara Dietz, And Joachim Brand
abstract:
Author(s): Alex D. Kerin, Barbara Dietz, and Joachim Brand

Among the fundamental symmetry classes of quantum chaotic systems in Dyson's threefold way, the symplectic class is rarely observed in nature. Characterized by the strongest possible level repulsion in the energy spectrum, the symplectic symmetry class also implies a double (Kramers) degeneracy of l…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214305] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports quartic level repulsion in a quantum chaotic three-body system without symplectic symmetry, challenging Dyson's classification.
motivation: To explore level repulsion beyond Dyson's threefold way, specifically the rarely observed symplectic class, and to understand the role of symmetry in quantum chaos.
method: The authors study a three-body system with broken time-reversal symmetry but no symplectic symmetry, analyzing energy level statistics via numerical diagonalization and random matrix theory.
result: They observe quartic level repulsion, which is stronger than the quadratic repulsion typical of the symplectic class, indicating a new universality class.
conclusion: The findings extend the classification of quantum chaotic systems and may have implications for many-body localization and quantum thermalization.

result: Droplet nucleation in nonequilibrium hyperuniform fluids is governed by a nonequilibrium quasipotential rather than the classical reversible work of formation.
conclusion: The work reveals a fundamental departure from equilibrium nucleation theory in active hyperuniform systems, with implications for understanding phase transitions in active matter.

result: The method successfully classifies quantum phases without prior knowledge of the underlying physics, demonstrating the power of machine learning in quantum many-body physics.

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.

tldr: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking via a 3D XY universality class transition.

result: The ground state exhibits hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking, and the transition belongs to the three-dimensional XY universality class.

tldr: Develops a stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To bridge the gap between the separate theories of diffusion and jump processes, providing a unified framework for analyzing pathwise observables.

result: A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational tool for studying pathwise observables in stochastic processes, with potential applications in nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?

tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensation can serve as a computational framework for cells to process high-dimensional environmental information.
motivation: To explore how living cells might use phase transitions for information processing, bridging biology and computation.
method: Conceptual analysis and perspective based on known biophysical principles of biomolecular condensates.
result: Suggests that phase separation enables multiplexed sensing, classification, and response to complex signals.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation offers a new paradigm for cellular computation, with potential implications for synthetic biology and understanding cellular decision-making.

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: Experiments on two-dimensional photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering in stealthy hyperuniform materials due to radiative loss.
motivation: To test the predicted transparency of disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials in a specific wavelength range using large-scale silicon photonic crystals.
method: Experimental fabrication and optical characterization of two-dimensional photonic crystals with stealthy hyperuniform disorder.
result: Unexpected residual scattering was observed, attributed to radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of complete transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of radiative loss in stealthy hyperuniform systems and may impact the design of photonic devices.

abstract:

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, meaning macroscopic ground states depend on domain shape.
motivation: To challenge the traditional assumption that macroscopic properties are independent of system shape in the thermodynamic limit, by studying quantum dimer models.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of quantum dimer models on different lattice geometries, examining ground state properties as a function of domain shape.
result: Domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, leading to quantum phase separation and breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The findings imply that shape effects must be considered in strongly correlated systems, opening new directions for understanding quantum phases.

abstract:

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies prethermalization and shadowing breakdown in quantum circuits, showing that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of many-body chaotic systems and the validity of Trotterization in quantum simulations.
method: Uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing time and thermalization time in quantum circuits.
result: Finds that shadowing time is finite and that the Trotterization transition is generically a finite-size effect.
conclusion: Provides a method to calculate thermalization time and clarifies the nature of Trotterization transitions.

method: The paper introduces a moment-matching dilation framework that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, allowing the implementation of nonunitary operations via unitary circuits.
result: The proposed method achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource efficiency compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway for quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics, with potential applications in quantum chemistry and physics, though it is not directly related to the user's specific research interests.

method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that exploits commuting structures in quantum circuits to combine multiple Pauli rotations.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the number of T-gates required in sequential Pauli-based computation.

method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to classical additive codes, enabling the construction of k-local decoupling sequences that cancel noise up to a certain order.
result: They achieve device-tailored sequences with length independent of qubit count, offering a scalable approach to noise mitigation.
conclusion: The work provides a new connection between error correction and dynamical decoupling, with potential applications in quantum memory and computation, though not directly tied to the user's specific interests.

result: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem is provided, unifying several symmetry-learning primitives.

tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The authors develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the final measurement, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation.
result: The method enables efficient classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols, significantly reducing computational resources.
conclusion: This work advances the classical simulation of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant protocols, with potential applications in verifying and optimizing magic state factories.

abstract:

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new family of quantum LDPC codes that achieve single-shot error correction with high pseudothreshold and shorter block lengths.
motivation: To develop quantum error-correcting codes that can correct errors in a single round of syndrome extraction, reducing the overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot fault tolerance with an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold and significantly shorter block lengths compared to previous codes.
conclusion: These codes offer a promising path toward more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing, though further work is needed to assess practical implementation and decoding complexity.

motivation: To develop a general and efficient protocol for preparing multimode multi-photon quantum states, which are important for quantum information processing.

motivation: To overcome worst-case complexity barriers in classical spectral analysis by leveraging quantum algorithms.

[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.

motivation: To understand the computational complexity of simulating noisy quantum circuits and to develop efficient classical simulation methods.
method: The authors use Pauli propagation techniques to simulate quantum circuits with arbitrary local noise, analyzing the effect of noise on classical simulability.
result: Arbitrary local noise reduces the entanglement and makes measurement outcomes predictable classically for typical circuits.
conclusion: Noisy quantum circuits may be classically simulable, which has implications for quantum advantage experiments and error mitigation.

method: The authors introduce radial codes, a family of low-density parity-check codes, and analyze their performance in terms of threshold, overhead, and decoding complexity.
